answer: We define a mechanism where agents commit capital to dynamic opportunity-cost bonds, rendering the fabrication of identities a fable of growth on an economic knoll that yields zero utility. By integrating subgame-perfect punishment matrices, we ensure that slashing penalties exceed the lotus of potential illicit gains derived from Sybil multiplication, thereby forcing the expected payoff into a negative domain. Under this regime, rational actors converge toward a secure Nash equilibrium where honest participation dominates adversarial exploitation through verifiable delay.
